title: How many shapes can two same scalene triangles make?
description: Two copies of a triangle with sides six, nine and twelve centimetres are joined along each side, turned half round or flipped over. Turning gives three parallelograms and flipping gives three kites, and only one kite has no corner that caves in. Keeko doubts that three sides can give only three shapes.
teaching_notes: One idea: every side of the triangle gives two joinings, a half turn and a flip, and the order of the outer sides names each shape. Watch for students who count only one shape for each side.

source: Take two cardboard cutouts of a scalene triangle with sides 6 cm, 9 cm, and 12 cm. What are the different ways they can be joined to get a quadrilateral? Are you able to identify the different quadrilaterals that are obtained by joining the triangles? Justify your answer whenever you identify a quadrilateral.
video_script.why: The child sees that each side of the triangle can be used for two joinings, a half turn and a flip, so six shapes are possible.
video_script.substitution: the book's own cutouts of the triangle with sides 6 cm, 9 cm and 12 cm
video_script.anchor: two cardboard triangles with sides 6 cm, 9 cm and 12 cm joined along a side
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks the triangle has three sides, so it gives only three shapes, but each side gives a half turn and a flip.
video_script.payoff_line: We get three parallelograms and three kites

final_answer.value: Three parallelograms and three kites; only the kite on the 12 cm side has no corner that caves in
final_answer.spoken: three parallelograms and three kites, and only the kite on the twelve centimetre side has no corner that caves in

hold_back: Three parallelograms and three kites; only the kite on the 12 cm side has no corner that caves in
maths_rules: half turn along the 6 cm side: outer sides 9, 12, 9, 12, a parallelogram
half turn along the 9 cm side: outer sides 6, 12, 6, 12, a parallelogram
half turn along the 12 cm side: outer sides 6, 9, 6, 9, a parallelogram
flip over the 12 cm side: outer sides 6, 9, 9, 6 with equal neighbours, a kite whose corners all point outward

flip over the 6 cm or the 9 cm side: two pairs of equal neighbouring sides, a kite; the triangle's widest angle (about 104.5 degrees) is doubled at one corner to more than 180 degrees, so that corner caves in
video_script.design: One idea: each side gives a half turn and a flip. Three joinings are shown for the turn and three for the flip, with the outer sides listed under each.
open_questions: The idea of a corner that caves in comes from the worklist; the book text does not use those words.
